Fire Initiation and Spread Resulting from a Nuclear Detonation over an Urban Area Meeting: 2020 Planning Guidance for Response to a Nuclear Detonation Location: Sandia Presenter: Jon Reisner Thanks: Eunmo Koo (LANL), ARA (Joe et al.), Alex Brown (Sandia), DTRA, DHS, and LDRD 08/27/19 Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Importance: Nuclear Weapons can Produce Large Fires/Storms § Of the 2 nuclear weapons denoted during WWII, a firestorm was produced in Hiroshima § Fire burned for several hours § Fire/Fallout/Rain were coupled, black rain was produced § Reports of people going into active fire zones (high radiation areas) to help put out fires/rescue individuals § Fire induced winds enhanced fallout in street canyons Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 2 Fire Initiation from a Nuclear Weapon § A significant amount of energy (approx. 40%) that reaches significant distances from the detonation is thermal § This energy can start fires… § But fires must survive shock wave and destruction of buildings (fuel) § Building construction and height of burst (HOB) makes a difference… § Wood buildings in Hiroshima & (HOB) were worst case for fire Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 3 Nuclear Weapon Fires-Source Term Probability of Ignition of Thick Fuels in LA from 100 KT (ARA-NucFast) Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 4 Sandia’s Solar Furnace Data Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 5 Refinement of Fire Initiation: Sandia’s Solar Tower § Investigates scaling from small spot size to larger size § Some materials that did not burn in solar furnace burned at tower § Tree burning was eye opening…imagine an entire forest being lit up Operated by TRIAD, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's NNSA Slide 6 Once Initiated… How do Fires Spread? § Definition: Movement of ongoing combustion from one location to another § Primary factors in spread (besides combustion): o Radiation o Convection (movement of air) o Conduction
